crime: That afternoon on the stairs, her friend told {WITCH_NAME} she wanted to spend less time together. “It's nothing,” she replied.

That evening they took their usual seats at the back of the recreation room for a film, apart from the other girls. Under the projector's noise, {WITCH_NAME} stabbed her friend beneath the ribs with a sharpened strip of metal, shrank the wound to a pinprick, and hid the blade in her sleeve.
When the lights came on, the girls walked past what looked like a sleeper. One returned to wake the friend and found her cold. With no obvious wound, they thought her heart had failed.

But beneath the jacket, a palm-sized bloodstain had dried around a tiny puncture. The wound had shrunk; the blood already spilled remained. The girls knew {WITCH_NAME}'s magic from the scrapes and burns she made small. She had been sitting beside her friend.
fields.epitaph: She called each loss nothing, until nothing was all she had.
fields.epithet: The Girl Who Called It Nothing
execution: A ring of needles surrounded her upright, bound body. Every minute the frame advanced, driving one needle a finger's depth into her before withdrawing it. She shrank each wound, but the damage it had already done remained. The needles continued, one by one, until she stopped moving.

magic.name: Pinchsmall
magic.text: She can shrink any injury until it is barely visible.
